title_original: Making Marie Antoinette review – sweet Coppola home movie reveals the family business
editorial_title_zh: 《造就玛丽·安托瓦内特》影评——温馨的科波拉家庭录像展现了家族事业
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这部由索菲亚的母亲埃莉诺拍摄的纪录片展现了拍摄古装片的一些压力，但它远不及她丈夫在《黑暗之心》中对他的动荡画像那样。索菲亚·科波拉主演基斯顿……的《玛丽·安托瓦内特》上映已有20年了……

article_text:
I t is 20 years since the release of Sofia Coppola’s Marie Antoinette starring Kirsten Dunst; it is a supportively unjudging, unironised study of the queen’s early years before the 1789 revolution, lavishly and accurately costumed, shot on location at Versailles and based on the Antonia Fraser biography – but also subversively and amusingly using pop tracks from the 70s and 80s on the soundtrack. It got a storm of booing from French critics, reportedly annoyed at the way their history had been reduced to a music video and fashion shoot with no French actors involved. Or hardly any.

In fact, for all the lack of political grit, the film was interesting and accomplished, and deservedly has a fanbase – and it is to that constituency that this making-of documentary from the director’s mother Eleanor Coppola is really addressed. It is basically a sweet family home movie on digital video which shows something of the strain and the longueurs of shooting a demanding period picture, but tactfully not seeing anything really explosive or bad-tempered. It is very far from Eleanor Coppola’s sensational behind-the-scenes film Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse about the tumultuous creation of Apocalypse Now, directed by her husband Francis Ford Coppola.

Eleanor and Sofia edited the footage together during the Covid lockdown and diary entries by Eleanor Coppola, who died in 2024, are sensitively read by Diane Lane. There are innumerable shots of Sofia smiling at her mother’s camera, yet sometimes looking a little tired and ill. Jason Schwartzman, playing Louis XVI, grins cheerfully, while Marianne Faithfull, as Empress Maria Theresa, cheerfully banters with Sofia in a very naughty English way. Francis Ford Coppola arrives at one stage and says that his advice to Sofia had been to “throw a Marie Antoinette party and invite everyone to come to it…” A good description of the film, actually.

Elsewhere, in Lane’s diary voiceover, Eleanor talks about the pain involved for her personally when Sofia all but broke off contact with her in her teen years, but Eleanor recognised that this was a process she had to go through before they became close again. Yet there is of course no hint of anything problematic here; this in effect is a very indulgent bonus feature, which in a DVD would come in at about 15 minutes, tops. But it does give what looks like a pretty faithful account of the patient slog needed to shoot a feature film.

"本稿では、ナカヤマン。の近年の芸術実践を概観したうえで、トークイベントで交わされた議論と、日本ギャラリーでの展示を参考に、《蓮葉の〜》の分析を試みる。加えて、本作を米国における日本の茶飲文化の受容史に文脈付け、とりわけ120年前にニューヨークのフォックス・ダフィールド社から記念碑的な英文著作『茶の本』を上梓した岡倉覚三（のち天心、1863〜1913）と比較検討することで、米国での日本文化発信活動が今日まで抱える、いまだ決着がついていない課題をいくつか提示したい。"}, メトロポリタン美術館に現れた献茶式

2026年6月7日、ニューヨークのメトロポリタン美術館の地下講堂にて、小さな献茶の儀が執り行われた。

講堂の床に敷かれた置き畳まで、すり足で登場した墨色の着物姿の男は、正座すると、帯に挟んだ紫色の帛紗（ふくさ）を抜き取り、それで茶器をひとつずつ丁寧に拭くことで、清めていく。男は茶釜のお湯を汲み、黒茶碗を清めると、不浄な水は、静かに建水に捨てられる。会場に並べられた椅子に着座する観覧者は、少し見下ろすような姿勢で、一連の点前を見守り、さらに男の頭上に設置された定点カメラの映像が会場前方のスクリーンに映し出されることで、事細かな動作が遠くからも確認できる。

ついに男は、茶杓で黒茶碗に抹茶を落とすと、お湯を注ぎ、茶筅で茶を点てる。仏前や霊前に供える茶は、茶筅で攪拌はしない、お茶湯がより一般的ではあるが、それでもここまでは、献茶式の体裁を保っていた。問題は結末である。緊張感のある点前の末に点てられた、特別なお茶の献じられた先にあったのは、ガンプラ（『機動戦士ガンダム』シリーズのプラモデル）である。そしてその隣には、なぜか真っ赤な薔薇の花びらが一片。さらに、畳際には、「GG」のロゴと「FAKE/NOT」の文字が入ったGUCCIのスニーカーが置かれている。開場時から、すでに講堂の前方に設置されていた簡易的な茶室空間において、これらのオブジェクトは、際立った存在感を放っていた。点前座のすぐ横に配置された杉蛤板の上に配置されたガンプラは、この献茶の儀の正客のようだ。ひょっとしたら、ガンプラにも八百万神（やおよろずのかみ）が宿り、神は茶の席では悪目立ちしそうなGUCCIのスニーカーでやってきたということだろうか？

じつは、ここまで記述してきたのは、《蓮葉の 繁る池水 所無み 旅空なる 人が宿さず (NØT) FLASH》（2026、以下《蓮葉の〜》）と題された、献茶式の形式をとったパフォーマンス作品であり、一連の儀式的な身ぶりを披露していた男は、現代アーティストのナカヤマン。（1974年京都市生まれ、海外ではYAMAN NKYMN名義で活動）だ。同作は、メトロポリタン美術館の日本ギャラリーで開催されている展覧会 「日本の陶芸の無限の芸術性（The Infinite Artistry of Japanese Ceramics）」 （1月19日〜2027年8月8日、5回の展示替えあり）に合わせて同美術館で開かれたトークイベントの締めくくりに披露された（＊1）。

本稿では、ナカヤマン。の近年の芸術実践を概観したうえで、トークイベントで交わされた議論と、日本ギャラリーでの展示を参考に、《蓮葉の〜》の分析を試みる。加えて、本作を米国における日本の茶飲文化の受容史に文脈付け、とりわけ120年前にニューヨークのフォックス・ダフィールド社から記念碑的な英文著作『茶の本』を上梓した岡倉覚三（のち天心、1863〜1913）と比較検討することで、米国での日本文化発信活動が今日まで抱える、いまだ決着がついていない課題をいくつか提示したい。

茶事を引用したリレーショナルアート作品

ナカヤマン。という風変わりな名前の現代アーティストは、2021年に京都の西本願寺内の国宝、飛雲閣で個展を開催し、本格的な作家活動を開始した。翌年には、フリーズ社とのコラボレーションで、ショートフィルムを2本発表している（＊2）。現代アーティストとしてのキャリアを始動する以前は、マーケティングストラテジストとして、ファッション業界などで活躍していたという。たしかに、作家デビュー以来、その戦略的な広報と、短期間で注目を集めるコンテンツ作りには、目まぐるしく移り変わるファッション市場で鍛え上げられた手腕が光る。

そして2023年にナカヤマン。は、茶美会（さびえ）という、これまでも革新的な茶会やイベントを企画してきた研究会のクリエイティブ・ディレクターに就任している。同年、京都の大徳寺芳春院で開催された個展では、「茶事を引用したリレーショナルアート作品」を発表し、翌年8月には、 森美術館 で開催された 「シアスター・ゲイツ展：アフロ民藝」 の関連イベントとして、茶美会の名義で、ゲイツ本人らと協力し、 特別な茶会を開いている （＊3）。さらに、現代アートとしての茶事を、2024年11月と25年12月には、ニューヨークの高級ホテル、ザ・マーサーでも発表している。一般的な茶事と同様に、3時間近い時間を要するナカヤマン。の「リレーショナルアート作品」は、完全招待制で、1日に3名程度の限られた観覧者に公開されてきた。メトロポリタン美術館での献茶式は、こうした近年の茶事形式の芸術実践の延長線上に位置付けられる。

ナカヤマン。が言及する「リレーショナルアート」とは、キュレーターのニコラ・ブリオーが、90年代以降に顕著となった、作品と鑑賞者の関係性や、鑑賞者同士の関係性を起点とする芸術実践をとらえる概念として、著作『関係性の美学』（1998）において提唱したものだ。たしかに、「一座建立」ともよく表現されるように、亭主と客が心を通わせることで、場を作り上げることを理想とする茶会は、制作者と参加する鑑賞者の関係性が生み出すリレーショナルアートと言えるかもしれない。さらに、献茶をリレーショナルアートの文脈に持ち込んだことは、作家・作品・鑑賞者という従来の相関図に、神仏や御霊という存在を新たに加える点で興味深い。

伝統への挑戦、あるいは回帰

とはいえ、《蓮葉の〜》は、それに先立って行われた作家による講演や、日本ギャラリーでの展覧会を参考に読解することで、いくつかの新鮮な視座を提供していることがわかる。

この展覧会を鑑賞してからナカヤマン。の献茶式に参加した筆者には、ミュージアム・ピースとなった茶道具をガラス越しに鑑賞する経験とは対照的に、《蓮葉の〜》は、それらのオブジェクトが失った意味や解釈を再び甦らせる行為のように映った。私たちは、メトロポリタン美術館のような考古物や古美術を中心に展示する空間において、視覚的オブジェクトから美的体験を得ることが一般的だ。しかし、茶会での美的体験は、五感を通じた経験によって作動されるものである。楽茶碗を実際に手に取り、さらに顔を近づけ、口を触れることで、視覚だけでなく、触覚、嗅覚、味覚を通して一服を楽しむことが、もともとは想定されていた。さらに静寂な茶室空間において、茶釜で湯がたぎる音（松風）や、露地の草木が風に揺れる音に耳を澄ませるなど、聴覚もまた茶会での美的体験において不可欠だ。《蓮葉の〜》は、美術館空間に介入し、オブジェクトが本来携えていた、目には見えない（不）視覚文化や、より拡張されたオブジェクトの見方を我々に改めて提示している。

加えて、ガンプラなどの現代的モティーフと献茶の融合は、利休や長次郎といった「わび茶」の先駆者たちへのオマージュとも解釈できる。ナカヤマン。とともに、トークイベントに登壇した十六代樂吉左衞門（1981年京都市生まれ）が指摘したように、初代長次郎が利休とともに創作した、手捏ねによる素朴な造形の楽茶碗は、いまでは伝統的と解釈されるが、豪華な唐物道具が重宝されていた16世紀においては、最先端の、まったく新しい茶碗であった。《蓮葉の〜》においても、ナカヤマン。は、積極的に最先端の茶道具を使用する利休の姿勢を踏襲している。

作家本人による講演で明かされたように、黒茶碗は、十六代樂吉左衞門による当代楽茶碗で、「萬代」という銘が付けられている（＊5）。さらにシアスター・ゲイツ造の水指は「艮門（うしとらもん）」、ナカヤマン。本人造の金の茶杓は「座屈」と命銘されている。八角系のステンレス製の皆具（杓立、建水、蓋置）は、金属彫刻作家の中村公子の作品だ。ガンプラを製造するバンダイや、『機動戦士ガンダム』に登場する「ザクII」を想起させる銘には、言葉遊びの感覚が見受けられる。さらに、鎮座するガンプラは、「ニュータイプ」という（ここでその詳述は割愛するが）概念が登場して以降のモデルで、GUCCIのスニーカーは、ナカヤマン。が敬愛するアレッサンドロ・ミケーレがクリエイティブ・ディレクター時代に発表した、ストリートカルチャーをラグジュアリーブランドに大胆に取り入れた作例だという。いずれも最先端を象徴的に示すアイテムである点において、長次郎の楽茶碗に通じるものがある。

十六代樂吉左衞門は、トークのなかで、自身は、初代が創出した茶碗を模して、まったく同じものを作る職人ではなく、楽茶碗、わび茶、そして伝統とは何か、現代において問い続けることで、独自の茶碗を作り上げることを志していると述べている。利休や長次郎が大成させた「わび茶」が、唐物名物を至上とした既存の価値体系を転換したことを鑑みれば、現代的な美意識の追求こそが、「わび茶」の伝統とも言える。「ニュータイプ」のガンプラや、最先端のファッションアイテムを献茶式に持ち込む《蓮葉の〜》は、一見、伝統への挑戦のようだが、実際には、伝統の革新性を抽出し、そこに回帰する試みでもあるのだ。

article_text:
Films and events

Galas

Behemoth!

BFI Patrons’ Gala

Michael Clayton director Tony Gilroy returns with a stylishly crafted portrait of a beguiling classical musician, played by Pedro Pascal.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Tony Gilroy

With Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett

USA 2026. 127min

Courtesy of Searchlight Pictures

Language English

Access information

Tuesday 13 October 18:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Wednesday 14 October 11:00

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Friday 16 October 15:20

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Cello prodigy Alex has spent his adult life changing orchestra chairs and lovers’ beds at regular intervals. On the run from his latest fling, he retreats to LA as a session player and into the suspended reality of a film score studio. Gilroy’s inventive script is rich in narrative textures, shape-shifting across time to explore the mysteries and complexities of the human heart. He’s ably supported by Pascal and a superb cast that includes Olivia Wilde and Will Arnett.

Kristy Matheson

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Congo Boy

Set in the Central African Republic, Rafiki Fariala’s melodic autobiographical feature follows a young refugee who, against all odds, chases his musical dreams.

The Man I Love

Ira Sachs cements his position as one of the great chroniclers of New York life with this tender, earthy portrait of the city’s gay scene in the 1980s.

The Liberation

In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader.

article_text:
Films and events

Journey

La Dérive

The debut of French New Wave filmmaker Paula Delsol fell into oblivion, but her essential contribution to cinema is now ready for rediscovery.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Paula Delsol

With Jacqueline Vandal, Paulette Dubost, Pierre Barouh

France 1964. 83min

Courtesy of Janus Films

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Jacquie, a beautiful 20-year-old, experiences various encounters with men in the south of France, where she returns to her family after leaving Paris. A young woman becoming the target of male predators is always a relevant topic. It’s presented here with a fresh approach: Jacquie is an unburdened wanderer rather than a desperate one, and her search for independence inebriating and joyful.

Giulia Saccogna

Restored in 4K in 2026 by La Cinémathèque française in collaboration with CNC – Centre national du cinéma et de l’image animée at TransPerfect Media laboratory, from the original 35mm picture and sound negatives. Funding provided by Neuflize OBC Corporate Foundation.

Content advice

Contains scenes of domestic violence or abuse.

Contains sexist attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Pakeezah

One of the last great classical musicals of Indian cinema, the visually opulent and emotionally tragic Pakeezah is a byzantine story of star-crossed lovers.

Gone to Earth

Long overshadowed within Powell and Pressburger’s canon, this major new restoration reveals the visual splendour and dramatic intensity of one of their most misunderstood films.

Ken Russell’s The Devils

Censored for over half a century, Ken Russell’s film returns in a landmark director’s cut reconstruction that reveals the full power of his original vision.

article_text:
When the Milwaukee Brewers face the Tampa Bay Rays in game one of the 122nd World Series tonight, they will be playing for more than just the right to hoist the sterling silver Commissioner’s Trophy after four wins. A rival museum’s Monet is also on the line.

The teams’ local art museums—the Milwaukee Art Museum , four miles east of where the Brewers play at American Family Field, and the Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, just over a mile west of the Rays’ Tropicana Field—have entered into a friendly wager, wherein the winning city’s museums earns the right to borrow a Monet painting from the loser’s collection.

The Milwaukee Art Museum is putting up Monet’s Waterloo Bridge, Sunlight Effect , ca. 1903, while the Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, is offering Houses of Parliament: Effect of Fog, London, 1904.

According to MAM’s website, Waterloo Bridge, Sunlight Effect is the one and only Monet in its collection, is a visitor favorite, and is currently on view at the museum. It was given to the museum by Mrs. Albert T. Friedmann upon her death in 1950, one of more than 40 objects she bequeathed to MAM. The painting is one of dozens Monet made painted during trips to London, showing a foggy view of a bridge across the River Thames in London, with smokestacks in the background.

Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg’s Monet is also one of the museum’s prized possessions. It’s currently on view in an upstairs gallery while its usual location, in the MFA’s collection gallery, is closed for installation. “For visiting Brewers fans, it might be their only chance to see it,” said MFA curator Stanton Thomas in a statement. Houses of Parliament: Effect of Fog, London was painted just a year after MAM’s canvas, and also shows buildings along the Thames. Monet made over a dozen plein-air paintings of London’s Houses of Parliament while on extended visits to the city in the early years of the 20th century.

This isn’t the first time the Milwaukee Art Museum has been involved in an art/sports crossover wager. In 2011, when the Green Bay Packers faced the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLV, MAM and the Carnegie Museum of Art in Pittsburgh entered into a similar loan arrangement based on the outcome of the game. After the Steelers lost (…to then Packers, current Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers) 31-25, CMA’s Pierre-Auguste Renoir painting Bathers With Crab traveled to Milwaukee for three months for MAM’s exhibition “Impressionism: Masterworks on Paper.” If the Steelers and the Packers ever meet again and the Steel Curtain prevails, maybe then the Carnegie will get its hand (temporarily) on MAM’s prized Gustave Caillebotte 1977 painting, Boating on the Yerres .
excerpt_original: Each museum's Monet was painted in the early 20th century and depicts scenes along the River Thames in London.

article_text:
Hollywood is struggling with layoffs and budget cuts, but entertainment just overtook the automotive industry to become the world’s second-largest business sector.

That’s according to consultancy Interbrand , whose latest Best Global Brands report pegs the cumulative value of entertainment companies at $332.5B, an increase of 12.4% year-on-year.

Within that, Netflix ‘s brand value grew 22%, which Interbrand considers as reflecting pushes into live entertainment, sport and advertising. That should be soothing mood music to Netflix execs, who’ve been under fire from Wall Street over its latest round of financials and for a lack of user engagement.

Related Stories

'Nobody Wants This' Has Netflix's Best Scripted Comedy Return Of The Year Despite 28% Audience Decline For Season 3 Debut

Netflix Lands 'AWOL' Dramedy From Craig Rowin, Goldstein & Daley's GoldDay

Netflix is ranked the 23rd most-value brand in the world, with Instagram, at seven, and YouTube , tenth, the only entertainment brands in the top ten overall. Disney is 23rd and Sony 35th, while Spotify is ranked 39th. Interbrand’s assessment is each has moved beyond their original role as a content platform and become businesses that shape consumer behavior.

Watch on Deadline

According to Gonzalo Brujó, Global CEO at Interbrand, “Entertainment’s growth reinforces one of the defining themes of this year’s ranking: Growth comes not from doing more, but from making stronger choices about where and how a brand creates value. In an industry where content is abundant and consumer attention is fragmented, competitive advantage is shifting from the scale of content to the strength of the brand.”

Brujó told Deadline that as AI “transforms how entertainment is created, distributed and consumed, technology alone will be an increasingly weaker source of differentiation,” and that “the brands that win will be those that understand the role of brand in driving choice, identify new arenas for growth, and consistently give people reasons to come back, creating habits, not just moments.”

Interbrand’s list was dominated by tech giants, with Apple top, Microsoft second, Google third, Amazon fourth and Samsung fifth. Other consumer brands such as McDonald’s, Toyota and Coca-Cola ranked highly, with Larry Ellison’s Oracle 13th. Gaming brands such as Nintendo and PlayStation also increased their brand values.

Omnicom-owned Interbrand’s annual report weights companies based on available financial data and requires them to have significant revenues outside their home territories, along with predictions of profits over the long-term and a ‘Brand Strenth Score’ equal to 50 or above. Research was conducted by Paradigm Sample.

article_text:
Feature

How Édouard Manet's Black Cat Became a Symbol of Modernity

Long associated with witchcraft and bad luck, the black feline became an emblem of artistic rebellion and urban life in 19th-century Paris.

Every Halloween, black cats return as emblems of witchcraft, bad luck, and the supernatural. Their sinister reputations stretch back centuries: starting in the Middle Ages, people associated cats with heresy and sexual transgression, and their perceived affinity with witches intensified during the trials of Elizabeth Francis and Agnes Waterhouse and their cat Sathan between 1565-1579.

But after the Enlightenment, 19th-century French artists and writers began to reclaim the mysterious and devilish qualities foisted onto felines as desirable. Alongside a new bourgeois pet-keeping culture, where caring for animals became associated with progress and enlightenment, bohemian artists and intellectuals began incorporating black cats into their work. The black cat became a symbol of independence and nonconformity, reflecting changing attitudes toward individualism and self-expression amid industrialization and urbanization. French writer and diplomat François-René de Chateaubriand described the cat’s modern independence favorably, stating , “What I like about the cat is his character, independent and almost heartlessness […] The cat lives alone, he has no need of society.” These inherited qualities of eroticism and defiance also became synonymous with the emerging language of modern art.

Art Institute of Chicago )

No painting or artist makes this transformation more apparent than Édouard Manet’s “Olympia” (1863). Historians like T.J. Clark have long hailed it as a “founding monument of modern art,” updating Titian’s “Venus of Urbino” (1534) with a stark depiction of a contemporary prostitute, her Black maid, and a black cat. The work provoked outrage at the Paris Salon in 1865: its subject matter, combined with flattened forms, bold color contrasts, and use of black, clearly rejected academic conventions. Critics latched onto the wiry black cat, whose arched back and luminous eyes seemed to embody the painting’s perceived vulgarity by showing what Olympia’s hand covered.

article_text:
Na Hong-jin regresa con una película tan ambiciosa como despareja, donde el terror, la acción y la ciencia ficción conviven a puro exceso.

Después de casi diez años, Na Hong-jin , director de The Chaser, The Yellow Sea y The Wailing, vuelve al cine con Hope , una gigantesca producción surcoreana que mezcla monstruos, ciencia ficción, acción, terror y humor negro.

Con 160 minutos de duración, la película es tan ambiciosa como irregular. Tiene momentos extraordinarios y otros en los que su exceso termina jugando en contra, pero pocas veces deja de resultar interesante.

Un misterio que se transforma en pesadilla

La historia comienza en un pequeño pueblo cercano a la frontera entre Corea del Sur y Corea del Norte. Después de encontrar una vaca brutalmente mutilada, el jefe de policía Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min) comienza a investigar lo ocurrido.

Lo que inicialmente parece el ataque de un animal salvaje rápidamente se transforma en algo mucho más extraño. Una criatura desconocida comienza a atacar a los habitantes y el pueblo queda atrapado en una situación que nadie comprende.

Uno de los grandes aciertos de Na Hong-jin está en retrasar la aparición del monstruo. Durante buena parte de la primera hora, la amenaza permanece prácticamente fuera de campo y el director construye el suspenso a través de edificios destruidos, vehículos destrozados, disparos y cuerpos.

Te puede interesar

Reseña de “Entrega al límite”: Alan Ritchson y Owen Wilson forman una gran dupla que sabe dar lecciones y no solo a los golpes

Reseña de “Wildwood: Bosque Salvaje”, una aventura de magia y amor familiar

La decisión funciona: antes de mostrar a la criatura, Hope consigue que el espectador imagine algo mucho peor.

Acción a toda velocidad

Cuando la película decide convertirse definitivamente en una producción de monstruos, Na Hong-jin despliega una enorme cantidad de recursos.

Las persecuciones y escenas de acción son uno de los grandes puntos fuertes. Hay vehículos, explosiones, enfrentamientos y secuencias filmadas con una energía impresionante, acompañadas por la fotografía de Hong Kyung-pyo, responsable de Parasite y Burning.

La cámara se mueve constantemente y consigue transmitir una sensación de caos controlado. A eso se suma la música de Michael Abels, que aporta tensión y convierte varias escenas en auténticos momentos de espectáculo.

Hoyeon se roba la película

El reparto es otro de los atractivos de Hope. Hwang Jung-min funciona muy bien como un policía que intenta sobrevivir a una situación que lo supera, mientras que Zo In-sung aporta una presencia más cercana al héroe tradicional.

Pero la gran sorpresa es Hoyeon.

La actriz demuestra un enorme dominio de las escenas de acción y, además, aprovecha el humor negro del guion para construir uno de los personajes más carismáticos de la película. Sus intervenciones aportan una energía particular y le permiten destacarse dentro de un elenco cargado de nombres internacionales.

El problema: cuando aparece el monstruo

Hope funciona especialmente bien mientras mantiene el misterio. Una vez que explica demasiado sobre sus criaturas y su origen, parte de la tensión inicial comienza a desaparecer.

Los efectos visuales tampoco son completamente consistentes. Algunas escenas resultan impresionantes, mientras que determinados momentos digitales tienen una apariencia demasiado artificial y contrastan con la espectacularidad de las secuencias prácticas.

El guion también deja personajes algo desdibujados y una segunda mitad que puede sentirse más larga de lo necesario.

Una película sobre el miedo al otro

Debajo de todo el espectáculo, Na Hong-jin introduce una lectura relacionada con el miedo a lo desconocido y la necesidad humana de encontrar un enemigo.

La cinta juega con la idea de que una comunidad puede reaccionar con violencia frente a aquello que no comprende. No es un concepto desarrollado con la profundidad de The Wailing, pero le aporta una capa interesante a una historia que, en principio, parece enfocada únicamente en monstruos y destrucción.

¿Vale la pena ver Hope?

Hope es una película excesiva, ambiciosa y bastante irregular. Su duración puede jugarle en contra y sus efectos visuales no siempre están a la altura de sus extraordinarias escenas de acción.

Pero también es una película con personalidad. Na Hong-jin vuelve con una propuesta que no tiene miedo de mezclar géneros, romper el tono y llevar el cine de monstruos hacia lugares inesperados.

Su primera hora es especialmente potente, Hoyeon se convierte en una de sus grandes revelaciones y algunas de sus secuencias de acción justifican por sí solas verla en pantalla grande.

Hope no es una película perfecta, pero sí una experiencia cinematográfica difícil de olvidar. Una enorme, extraña y desquiciada apuesta de Na Hong-jin que seguramente dará mucho de qué hablar.

Calificación: 7.5/10. Estreno: 8 de octubre en cines, luego en MUBI .

article_text:
毎年一度の「開封」に合わせて開催される「正倉院展」の季節になりました。今年は、奈良国立博物館での「正倉院展」に加え、皇居三の丸尚蔵館のグランドオープンを記念した特別展でも、1300年の時を超えて守り伝えられた正倉院宝物が公開されます。奈良で、東京で、貴重な宝物を鑑賞できる特別な年になりそうです。

奈良博「第78回正倉院展」 “龍のミイラ”も！？

今年の正倉院展では、ポスターにもデザインされた聖武天皇ゆかりの「 漆胡瓶 」（北倉43）など60件が出展されます。うち初出陳は11件。

漆胡瓶は、西方のペルシアに由来する形の水差しで、東アジアの漆工の技術を用いて作られており、当時の東西交流を象徴する宝物です。淡い緑色がさわやかな「白瑠璃瓶」（中倉69）や、花をくわえた鳥が愛らしい象牙の碁石「 紅牙撥鏤碁子 」「 紺牙 撥鏤碁子」（北倉25）など、当時のみごとな技や美意識に触れられます。

18年ぶりに公開される異色の宝物「 虹龍 」（南倉174）も話題を集めそうです。室町時代に将軍が「 竜日干 」を見たという記録が残っており、これに該当するとされているミイラで、近年の研究で体型や歯の特徴などからニホンテンと判明しました。宝庫に侵入したのちに自然乾燥したのか、ミイラを龍に見立てて納入したかは不明だそうです。

正倉院展は10月24日（土）から11月9日（月）までで、会期中無休。事前に日時指定予約が必要です。通常より早い午前8時からの鑑賞や、月～木曜は午後4時以降、金・土・日曜と祝日は午後5時以降に入館できる「レイト割」のチケットも好評販売中です。

初の皇居内一般公開 螺鈿紫檀琵琶など11件

建て替えのため休館中の皇居三の丸尚蔵館（東京・皇居東御苑内）では、11月3日のグランドオープンに合わせ、記念の特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」が開幕します。皇室ゆかりの収蔵品から選りすぐりの優品が紹介されますが、11月23日（月・祝）までの前期展示では、正倉院宝物も展示されることになりました。皇居内での一般公開は初めてです。

聖武天皇ご遺愛の品々をまとめた「国家珍宝帳」に記載されている「 七條褐色 紬袈裟 」（北倉1‒2）は、光明皇后が東大寺大仏に献納した宝物のうちの1点。「 螺鈿紫檀琵琶 」（北倉27）、「 八角鏡 平螺鈿背 」（北倉42-7）は、いずれもヤコウガイによる螺鈿の装飾がいまも美しく輝いています。古代の工芸技術の粋が凝らされた逸品は見逃せません。

動物たちの姿が愛らしい「 﨟纈屛風 羊木屛風 ・ 熊鷹屛風 」（北倉44）、美しい鞘の「 犀角把 白銀葛形鞘 珠玉荘刀子 」（中倉131-7）など多彩な計11件が並びます。正倉院に伝わった絹織物を貼り交ぜた「 赤地唐花文 錦等雑貼 （古屛風 第六十号 第六扇）」（南倉179）は、皇居内で育てられた赤色の染料「日本茜」と、「小石丸」の絹糸を用いて再現された「模造 赤地唐花文錦」もあわせて展示されます。

皇居三の丸尚蔵館グランドオープン記念特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」は2027年1月24日（日）まで。日時指定制で、会場での当日券の販売はありません。チケットの購入や中期、後期の展示作品の確認は 特設ウェブサイト で。

editorial_title_zh: 切鲁蒂基金会：为藏品带来全新声音与叙事
editorial_excerpt_zh: 切鲁蒂基金会推出了一项特别开放日的新计划以及全新项目，旨在讲述并分享其图书、家具、地毯和艺术品收藏。特别是10月30日星期五，在其位于里沃利别墅的总部，它……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "都灵艺术周期间推出的创新项目之一是《Fonogrammi》 ，这是一系列由艺术家、音乐家、艺术史学家和作家构思的全新声音委托创作，他们应邀通过前所未有的音频路线来诠释切鲁蒂藏品。这些干预打破了传统导览的形式，成为声音表演的舞台，融合了音乐创作和受藏品路线启发的叙事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，值此马里萨·梅尔茨（Marisa Merz）大型三地展览——在里沃利城堡、梅尔茨基金会和GAM举办、并将持续至2027年4月4日的《INTERFERENZE #7: MARISA MERZ 》——之际，两位都灵艺术家的作品在艺术周期间被纳入了藏品。该项目将藏品与当代艺术联系起来，其路线将包括一件雕塑（《无题》，无年代），它与阿尔贝托·贾科梅蒂（Alberto Giacometti）、阿图罗·马蒂尼（Arturo Martini）和梅达尔多·罗索（Medardo Rosso）的作品展开对话；还有一件纸本作品（《无题》，2010-2012），被放置在一幅弗朗西斯·培根（Francis Bacon）的画作旁，从而创造出新的搭配。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Fondazione-Cerruti-2-724x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Marisa Merz, Senza titolo, 2010-2012", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "直至2027年2月28日，由卢卡·切纳（Luca Cena）策展的《Palinsesti》第二篇章也在展出中，旨在重新发掘藏品中的图书核心。通过《PALINSESTI #2: PERFECT BINDING 》 ，这些珍贵的版本被从图书馆的书架上取下，分布在别墅的各间房间里。这些带有手工装订封面的卷册可追溯至15世纪至20世纪，构成了切鲁蒂遗产的重要部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最后，通过《UNICUM》 ，人们将目光聚焦于一件特定的物品，将其从原本的上下文中剥离出来，并在一条包含与该主题相关的其他艺术品和物品的路线中进行展示。该项目由专家主导，在第一版《UNICUM #1》中，艺术史学家、伊斯兰和印度艺术专家比阿特丽斯·坎皮（Beatrice Campi）对一张萨法维丝绸地毯进行了深入探讨。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Fondazione-Cerruti_Palisesti2_Perfect-Binding_Studio1_Ph.-Silvia-Mangosio-Luca-Vianello-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Fondazione Cerruti, Palisesti2, Perfect Binding Studio1. Ph. Silvia Mangosio, Luca Vianello", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "关于《Fonogrammi》，首期邀请了比阿特丽斯·博尼诺与Any（Beatrice Bonino x Any）、杰瑞米·戴勒（Jeremy Deller）、乔治·迪·多梅尼科（Giorgio Di Domenico）和锡翁·帕金森（Siôn Parkinson）。创作者们制作了四份语音导览，可从基金会网站下载，并在切鲁蒂别墅及其他地方收听。在此次艺术周期间，他们的声音表演在Cripta747进行了现场呈现，带来《THE PHONOGRAMS VARIETY SHOW》 。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过将切鲁蒂的宇宙带入自2008年以来一直支持当代艺术研究和创作的独立文化中心，艺术家们由此实现了弗朗西斯·费代里科·切鲁蒂（Francesco Federico Cerruti）让其珍贵藏品得以被公众访问的愿望。当晚的活动分为四个乐章，开场是《Any Lamentation (The Lowest Level of the Human Mood)》 ，这是一首为竖琴创作的电声作品，由Any创作（音乐家阿纳斯塔西娅·帕特利斯 Anastasia Patellis的艺名），并与艺术家比阿特丽斯·博尼诺（Beatrice Bonino）展开对话。这场表演探索并用声音翻译了切鲁蒂的世界，还原了他每次购买行为背后隐藏的渴望、满足与不安。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "竖琴的音符将听众包裹在一个空灵的氛围景观中，该景观由简短的声音序列构建，这些序列循环重复，缓慢地重叠和分层。于是，渴望呈现出一种持续张力的形态，类似于一种悬置的哀歌，似乎永远无法找到完全的解决。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Jeremy-Deller-at-Collezione-Cerruti-1024x768.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Jeremy Deller at Collezione Cerruti", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "演出随后继续，带来了由乔治·迪·多梅尼科（Giorgio Di Domenico）讲述的《Desired Objects: Desire and Desires in the Cerruti Collection》 ，他对弗朗西斯·费代里科·切鲁蒂的世界及其藏品作品进行了历史解读。讲述穿梭于渴望的不同色调之中：从激发收藏行为的热情，到对拥有的痴迷，再到被铭记和被爱的需求。藏品作为一种深刻且包罗万象的关系的观念也浮现出来，人们很难与之分离。收藏家的愿望就这样与艺术家们的愿望交织在一起，通过对切鲁蒂所购作品的重新解读，深入探究其意义和可能的诠释。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "紧随其后的是锡翁·帕金森（Siôn Parkinson）的《Antechamber: A Musical》 ，这是一场声音表演，其中罗比·唐纳德（Robbie Donald）的风笛声成为了帕金森歌唱与噪声交织的基础。由此诞生了一个悬置的时刻，一个类似于前厅的空间。别墅由此被带到了Cripta747，化作了一份总谱，而帕金森的声音则在其墙壁之间回荡。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为当晚画上句号的是杰瑞米·戴勒（Jeremy Deller），他带来了一场伴有视频和背景音乐朗读的表演，这些音乐汲取自档案馆资料以及别墅和切鲁蒂的历史，为藏品赋予了声音。这是一场从英格兰东海岸一直延伸至别墅图书馆的旅程。叙事的起点是诺福克的一个村庄，由戴勒在藏品中保存的约翰与威廉·布劳（John and William Blaeu）1662年出版的17世纪地图集《大地图集》（The Grand Atlas）中锁定，这也是艺术家经常造访的地方。正是从那里，戴勒录制了一部分故事，让一个曾险些波及核电站的大火所重创的村庄历史重见天日。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Any-Mothclub-London.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Any Mothclub London", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "凭借纪录片制作大师般的娴熟手法，德勒将历史碎片与个人记忆交织在一起，构建出一部全新的作品：一段似乎旨在赋予切鲁蒂的故事以连续性与关怀的叙事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这正是切鲁蒂基金会项目所秉持的精神，该基金会旨在遵照其创始人弗朗切斯科·费德里科·切鲁蒂（Francesco Federico Cerruti）的遗愿，保护并提升其收藏的价值。切鲁蒂基金会正稳步推进开放与重振的历程，致力于让公众能够更加便捷地欣赏其收藏——这些藏品珍藏于里沃利山丘上的别墅中。这是一个跨越中世纪至当代数个世纪艺术史的折衷主义收藏，并且正日益向与当下的对话敞开更多契机。弗朗切斯科·费德里科·切鲁蒂出生于热那亚，出身于中产阶级家庭，他从父亲以及从事工业装订的家族生意中体会到了勤勉与劳作的价值。正是在此基础上，他开启了自己作为收藏家的历程——这是他那个时代最为精致的收藏之一，由其个人且鲜明的品味所指引。如今，切鲁蒂别墅内藏有书籍、艺术品和家具，其陈设方式完全依照他当年的设想，向公众呈现的不仅是一场收藏，更是其创造者的世界与愿景。", Il punto di partenza della narrazione è un villaggio del Norfolk, individuato da Deller nell’atlante seicentesco di John e William Blaeu, il Grande Atlante del 1662, conservato nella Collezione e luogo che l’artista frequenta abitualmente. Proprio da lì Deller ha registrato parte del racconto, riportando alla luce la storia del villaggio, segnato da un incendio che ha rischiato di coinvolgere una centrale nucleare."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/Any-Mothclub-London.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Any Mothclub London", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Con la maestria di un documentarista, Deller intreccia frammenti di storia e ricordi personali, costruendo una nuova composizione: un racconto che sembra voler dare continuità e cura alla storia di Cerruti."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ed è proprio questo lo spirito che anima i progetti della Fondazione Cerruti, nata per conservare e valorizzare la sua collezione, nel rispetto delle volontà testamentarie del suo fondatore, Francesco Federico Cerruti . La Fondazione Cerruti porta avanti un percorso di apertura e rilancio, volto a rendere sempre più accessibile al pubblico la sua Collezione, custodita nella Villa sulle colline di Rivoli. Una raccolta eclettica che attraversa secoli di storia dell’arte, dal Medioevo alla contemporaneità, e che si apre sempre più a nuove occasioni di dialogo con il presente. Nato a Genova e proveniente da una famiglia di ceto medio, Francesco Federico Cerruti aveva appreso dal padre e dall’attività di famiglia, dedicata alla legatoria industriale, il valore della diligenza e del lavoro. Da qui ha avuto inizio il suo percorso di collezionista, uno dei più raffinati del suo tempo, guidato da un gusto personale e ben definito. article_text:
Una delle novità proposte durante la Torino Art Week è il progetto Fonogrammi , una nuova serie di commissioni sonore ideate da artisti, musicisti, storici dell’arte e scrittori, invitati a interpretare la Collezione Cerruti attraverso inediti percorsi audio. Gli interventi scardinano la forma della tradizionale visita guidata, diventando teatro di performance sonore, tra composizioni musicali e narrazioni ispirate al percorso della Collezione.

Inoltre, in occasione della grande mostra dedicata a Marisa Merz in tre sedi, Castello di Rivoli, Fondazione Merz e GAM, con INTERFERENZE #7: MARISA MERZ , in programma fino al 4 aprile 2027, due opere dell’artista torinese sono state inserite nella Collezione per l’Art Week. Il programma, che mette in relazione la Collezione con l’arte contemporanea, vedrà nel percorso una scultura (Senza titolo, n.d.) che dialoga con quelle di Alberto Giacometti , Arturo Martini e Medardo Rosso , e un’opera su carta (Senza titolo, 2010-2012), collocata accanto ad un dipinto di Francis Bacon , creando nuovi accostamenti.

Fino al 28 febbraio 2027 è in mostra anche il secondo capitolo di Palinsesti , a cura di Luca Cena per riscoprire il nucleo librario della Collezione. Con PALINSESTI #2: PERFECT BINDING , le rare edizioni pregiate sono state prelevate dagli scaffali della biblioteca e distribuite tra le stanze della Villa. I volumi, con copertine rilegate a mano e databili dal Quattrocento al Novecento, rappresentano una parte importante dell’eredità di Cerruti.

Infine, con UNICUM , è stata posta l’attenzione su un particolare oggetto, isolato dal contesto originario e messo in mostra in un percorso insieme ad altre opere e oggetti legati allo stesso tema. Il progetto è guidato da specialisti e, per questa prima edizione, UNICUM #1, Beatrice Campi, storica dell’arte ed esperta di arte islamica e indiana, ha proposto un approfondimento su un tappeto safavide in seta.

A proposito di Fonogrammi, per la prima edizione sono stati invitati Beatrice Bonino x Any, Jeremy Deller, Giorgio Di Domenico e Siôn Parkinson. Gli autori hanno realizzato quattro audioguide, scaricabili dal sito della Fondazione e ascoltabili in Villa Cerruti e altrove. Durante questa Art Week, le loro performance sonore sono state presentate dal vivo a Cripta747, con THE PHONOGRAMS VARIETY SHOW .

Trasportando l’universo di Cerruti all’interno del centro culturale indipendente che dal 2008 sostiene la ricerca e la produzione artistica contemporanea, gli artisti hanno così esaudito il desiderio di Francesco Federico Cerruti di rendere accessibile la sua preziosa Collezione. La serata si è articolata in quattro atti, aprendosi con Any Lamentation (The Lowest Level of the Human Mood) , la composizione elettroacustica per arpa, realizzata da Any, nome d’arte della musicista Anastasia Patellis, in dialogo con l’artista Beatrice Bonino. La performance ha esplorato e tradotto in suono l’universo di Cerruti, restituendo il desiderio, la soddisfazione e l’inquietudine che si celavano dietro ognuno dei suoi acquisti.

Le note dell’arpa hanno avvolto gli ascoltatori in un paesaggio ambient rarefatto, costruito attraverso brevi sequenze sonore che si ripetevano ciclicamente, sovrapponendosi e stratificandosi lentamente. Il desiderio ha così assunto la forma di una tensione costante, simile a un lamento sospeso, che sembrava non trovare mai una piena risoluzione.

Lo spettacolo è proseguito con Desired Objects: Desire and Desires in the Cerruti Collection , la narrazione di Giorgio Di Domenico, che ha proposto una lettura storica dell’universo di Francesco Federico Cerruti e delle opere della sua Collezione. Il racconto ha attraversato le diverse sfumature del desiderio: dalla passione che anima l’atto del collezionare fino all’ossessione del possesso, passando per il bisogno di essere ricordati e amati. È emersa anche l’idea della Collezione come una relazione profonda e totalizzante, dalla quale risulta difficile separarsi. Le aspirazioni del collezionista si sono così intrecciate con quelle degli artisti, attraverso una rilettura delle opere acquisite da Cerruti, indagate nei loro significati e nelle loro possibili interpretazioni.

È seguito Antechamber: A Musical di Siôn Parkinson, una performance sonora in cui il suono della cornamusa scozzese di Robbie Donald è diventato la base per un intreccio di canto e sonorità noise di Parkinson. Ne è nato un momento sospeso, uno spazio simile a un’anticamera. La Villa è stata così trasportata fino a Cripta747, trasformata in una partitura, mentre la voce di Parkinson riecheggiava tra le sue pareti.

A chiudere la serata è stato Jeremy Deller con una lettura accompagnata da un video e da un accompagnamento sonoro di sottofondo che, attingendo a materiali d’archivio e alla storia della Villa e di Cerruti, ha dato voce alla collezione. Un viaggio dalla costa orientale dell’Inghilterra fino alla biblioteca della Villa. Il punto di partenza della narrazione è un villaggio del Norfolk, individuato da Deller nell’atlante seicentesco di John e William Blaeu, il Grande Atlante del 1662, conservato nella Collezione e luogo che l’artista frequenta abitualmente. Proprio da lì Deller ha registrato parte del racconto, riportando alla luce la storia del villaggio, segnato da un incendio che ha rischiato di coinvolgere una centrale nucleare.

Con la maestria di un documentarista, Deller intreccia frammenti di storia e ricordi personali, costruendo una nuova composizione: un racconto che sembra voler dare continuità e cura alla storia di Cerruti.

Ed è proprio questo lo spirito che anima i progetti della Fondazione Cerruti, nata per conservare e valorizzare la sua collezione, nel rispetto delle volontà testamentarie del suo fondatore, Francesco Federico Cerruti . La Fondazione Cerruti porta avanti un percorso di apertura e rilancio, volto a rendere sempre più accessibile al pubblico la sua Collezione, custodita nella Villa sulle colline di Rivoli. Una raccolta eclettica che attraversa secoli di storia dell’arte, dal Medioevo alla contemporaneità, e che si apre sempre più a nuove occasioni di dialogo con il presente. Nato a Genova e proveniente da una famiglia di ceto medio, Francesco Federico Cerruti aveva appreso dal padre e dall’attività di famiglia, dedicata alla legatoria industriale, il valore della diligenza e del lavoro. Da qui ha avuto inizio il suo percorso di collezionista, uno dei più raffinati del suo tempo, guidato da un gusto personale e ben definito. Oggi Villa Cerruti contiene libri, opere d’arte e arredi disposti così come lui stesso li aveva immaginati, restituendo al pubblico non soltanto una collezione, ma anche il mondo e la visione di chi l’ha creata.

article_text:
Mahershala Ali broke down in tears on stage at the BFI London Film Festival on Saturday as he recalled the young boy at the heart of “Moonlight.”

The Barry Jenkins drama won him one of his two Oscars and recently marked its 10th anniversary.

During a Screen Talk hosted by Amon Warmann, Ali was discussing the dinner-table scene in which young Chiron asks Juan, the drug dealer Ali plays, whether he sells drugs. “You see this like crisis for this young boy who’s already in crisis,” he said. “It’s really heartbreaking.”

When Warmann asked what accounted for the film’s enduring power, Ali paused, overcome with emotion and wiping away tears. “Sorry, just need a second,” he said.

Popular on Variety

“Any time people put flesh on the bones of those who haven’t been seen or had their moment, I think it’s important,” he said once he had composed himself. “I think ‘Moonlight’ was able to make those characters people… make it personal.”

To play Juan, Ali drew on a man he had known all his life, an uncle-like figure he had grown up playing basketball with who also worked as a substitute teacher. The man was arrested and sent to prison while Ali was in college, which left the actor stunned.

“I thought of him a lot in the making of the film because of how human everyone was in my environment and in my upbringing,” Ali said.

He was candid about the backlash that followed “Green Book,” in which he played pianist Don Shirley opposite Viggo Mortensen. It was his first role of that magnitude, and the backlash included the controversy over what Shirley’s family had and hadn’t sanctioned.

“I still stand by it. I stand by the work,” Ali said, adding that he also stands by “the experience as a whole, and what it taught me.”

Ali, who won his second Oscar for the role, described going from feeling like a golden boy to wondering what he had done wrong. “I think I’m just sensitive in general, you know what I mean? So it definitely like had its impact, like for sure,” he said, adding that he was grateful for the exposure. “Like swords are folded in the fire, you know?”

Of his back-to-back Oscar wins, Ali said: “I felt a sense of accomplishment, which is not fulfillment.” He keeps the statuettes in a cabinet, out of his sight line, so he could get back to work.

Ali voices Aaron Davis in the animated “Spider-Verse” films, including a version of the character from another universe who appears at the end of “Across the Spider-Verse” and returns in “Beyond the Spider-Verse.” Asked how he tells the two apart, he said: “I don’t want to give anything away or spoil anything, I’ve got to be careful.” Pressed on whether he had finished recording, he joked: “I might not even be in it, man! I don’t know, man! I don’t know!”

He was more forthcoming about the process. Actors are filmed in the booth, and their improvised moments often make it into the finished film, sometimes prompting rewrites and extra recording sessions. “I think that’s why, honestly, the animation films will hold up better than live-action films,” Ali said.

The actor went straight from “Green Book” into “True Detective,” with only a week or two off, to play detective Wayne Hays across three timelines. Playing the older Hays meant 80-hour weeks, with four hours in the makeup chair from 3:30 a.m. The shoot ran seven months, and his daughter was a year old at the time.

“I just think about how I almost went crazy doing that part,” he said.

Two of Ali’s films are screening at the festival. He voices bandit leader Brendan in the animated “Wildwood.” In action thriller “Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother,” he plays Latif, a devout Muslim father and contract killer, and had three or four days to learn the fight choreography.

“It’s really more like dance than what people realize,” he said.

On playing a Black Muslim father, Ali said: “I don’t feel like Black fathers have the dimensionality that I would love for them to have.”

Now at work on the HBO series “Task” with Mark Ruffalo, Ali said he feels “exhausted for the right reasons” and “tired in the right way.”

“So that’s why I feel like I’m just getting started,” he said.

title_original: 【特別ルポ】歌舞伎俳優の大谷廣松さんと東京都現代美術館の企画展「共時的星叢──時を共にした星たち　越境する芸術のまなざし」に行ってきました。その③－「歌舞伎役者は子供のころから『伝統』が体に染み込んでいるので、新しいものを受け入れるのに抵抗がないんですよ」
editorial_title_zh: 【特别报道】我们和歌舞伎演员大谷广松一起参观了东京都现代美術館的企划展“共时性星丛——共度时光的群星：越境艺术的目光”。其之三——“歌舞伎演员从小‘传统’就深入骨髓，所以对接受新事物毫无抵抗力。”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 本次“特别报道”聚焦东京都现代美术馆的“共时性星丛——共度时光的群星：越境艺术的目光”。这是延续自上期歌舞伎演员大谷广松与客座策展人黄亚历之间的对话，而对于身为传统艺术传承人的广松来说……

"美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——担任本次“特别报道”嘉宾的大谷广松先生是一位歌舞伎演员，在21世纪的今天，他一边传承传统，一边置身于实时演艺的前线。黄先生看过歌舞伎吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 我对日本的传统文化艺术很感兴趣，也想了解它是如何发展并延续至今的。所以真的很想看一次歌舞伎的舞台表演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——以歌舞伎世界为背景的电影《国宝》（李相日导演）去年上映了，不仅在日本，在很多国家也引发了话题，您看过了吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 我在来日本的飞机上看了。是一部挺长的电影，不过正好赶上飞行时间（笑）。我当时想的是，当新风吹进传统社会时，人们究竟是如何应对的。不仅仅是电影所处的时代，我想现代也会有这种状况，所以我也对此产生了兴趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——也就是如何让“传统”与“革新”这两者并存，对吧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "黄亚历。“对日本动漫之类的不太感兴趣”", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "广松 歌舞伎独特的“家”之系统，我认为这就是对该问题的一个答案。我们在演员的“家”中长大，戏剧或者说歌舞伎自然而然地深入了我们的骨髓。所以该怎么说呢，对于新事物、“革新”，我们几乎没有什么抗拒感。即使我们将这种“革新”带到舞台上并融入作品中，最终呈现出来的东西也全都会变成“歌舞伎”。我们能够通过歌舞伎这一滤镜来处理所有事物。最近，我们也把《ONE PIECE》和《火影忍者-NARUTO-》这类漫画原作的作品搬上了舞台，但只要由我们来演，就必然会变成歌舞伎。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——现在的歌舞伎虽然被认为是传统艺术，但回溯到江户时代，它可是积极吸收了时尚、音乐、风俗等最前沿元素的存在呢。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "广松 虽然也有一些比较保守、讨厌引入这种“最前沿”的人，但演员本身往往并不觉得有什么。基本上歌舞伎是大众艺术，只要“能让观众高兴，什么都行”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——在21世纪的今天，说到日本发起的大众文化，就会想到动漫，或者是奥特曼、假面骑士等英雄作品，从这个意义上讲，它与歌舞伎的亲和性其实很高呢。战前被称为名演员的第十五代市村羽左卫门甚至有一种说法称其祖先有法国血统，歌舞伎这个世界或许比人们普遍想象的还要灵活且胸怀广阔。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "广松表示，“歌舞伎演员对‘新事物’意外地没有违和感”", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w5.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展览现场。黄土水《释迦出山》 1997年铸造（基于1926年石膏原模） 台北市立美术馆藏", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "广松 听说台湾现在日本动漫也很受欢迎。黄先生以前也看过动漫吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 我其实不太关注。不过对于只有日本动漫受欢迎、台湾本土原创角色很难成长现状，我倒觉得多少有点问题。最近台湾的漫画家也越来越多了，我觉得他们也都在努力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "广松 从这些方面来看，我觉得日本和台湾的人们作为同属于东亚的居民，确实有相通的地方。正如我刚才所说，正因如此，我觉得这次展览有很多值得我们学习的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展览现场。〈何谓故乡／我〉", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w7.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "陈澄波《戴绿面具的裸妇》 1929～1933年 私人藏", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——纵观整个展览，对于这个时期台湾与日本的交流，您有什么感想吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 促成这次展览契机的，是我对诞生于1930年代的台湾诗人群体“风车诗社”产生了兴趣。据说“风车诗社”将超现实主义带入了台湾文坛，在这个时代，台湾的表达者们通过日本这一滤镜，尝试了各种风格。我们真的能用西方的方法去将其归类整理吗？我觉得这样做未免有些过于简单粗暴了。我希望大家能以原本的形式去看看当时日本与台湾究竟是以何种形式进行了怎样的交流。希望大家能暂时忘却“西方的概念”，从每位观展者自己的思考出发，去重新审视这些交流究竟是怎样的，我是这么想的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "广松 这大概也是反映了黄先生的这种想法吧，每个作品的解说虽然通俗易懂且十分细致，但又没有强加某种特定的观点，给人一种很平易近人的感觉。日本艺术家和台湾艺术家之间有着怎样的关系，这种联系也一目了然。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 日本统治时期的台湾有着各种限制，日本人和台湾人的地位也不一样。去日本本身就是一件很费劲、很困难的事情。在当时，台湾农民的生活并不富裕，可以说是饱受苦难。文学家赖和看到这一幕痛彻心扉，并将他们的生活写了下来。当时有富有的人、贫穷的人，有各种阶级的人，也有各自的创作与作品。即便经济上不那么宽裕，也有人在赞助人的支持下继续创作，从而过着不愁生计的生活。在展览中，我们希望将这些状况原原本本地呈现出来，传达出“共时性”这一信息。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "广松 这种想法正是这种平实感的来源吧。这是一个能以与以往美术展不同的形式激发智性与感性的展览。对我和而言也是一次非常有趣的体验。（完）", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今回の「特別ルポ」は、東京都現代美術館の「共時的星叢──時を共にした星たち 越境する芸術のまなざし」。前回から続く歌舞伎役者の大谷廣松さんとゲストキュレーターの黄亜歴さんとの対話だが、伝統芸能の継承者である廣松さんにとって、ここで紹介される「伝統と革新」というテーマは身近な存在。そこをひとつのキーワードとして、話は広がっていった。（文・田中聡、写真・青山謙太郎、通訳・白仕偉）"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "〈翻訳と創造のはざまで〉の展示の前で。左の作品は、藤島武二《台南風景》（1933年、神奈川県立近代美術館蔵）", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――「特別ルポ」を担当していただいている大谷廣松さんは歌舞伎役者であり、21世紀の今、伝統を継承しながらリアルタイムの芸能の現場に身を置く存在でもあります。黄さんは歌舞伎をご覧になったことはありますか？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 日本の伝統的な文化芸能には興味がありますし、それがどんなふうに発展し、現在存在しているかも、知りたいと思っています。だから歌舞伎の舞台はぜひ見たいですね"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――歌舞伎の世界を舞台にした映画『国宝』（李相日監督）が昨年公開されまして、日本だけでなくいろいろな国で話題になっているんですが、ご覧になりましたか？"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 日本に来る飛行機の中で見ました。結構長い映画なんですが、フライトの時間にはちょうどよかった感じで（笑）。見ていて思ったのは、伝統ある社会に新しい風が入るとき、どんな風に対処していたのだろうか、ということ。この映画の舞台となっている時代だけでなく、現代でもそういう状況はあると思いますので、そこにも興味を持ちました"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――「伝統」と「革新」、このふたつをどのように両立させるか、ということですね"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "黄亜歴さん。「あまり日本のアニメなどには興味がなかった」", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "廣松 歌舞伎独特の「家」というシステムが、それに対する答えのひとつだと思います。役者の「家」で育つ私たちは、自然に芝居、というか歌舞伎が体に染み込んでいるんです。だからというか何というか、新しいもの、「革新」に対する抵抗感はほとんどないんです。私たちがその「革新」を舞台上に持ち込んで、それを作品に取り入れたとしても、出来上がったものはすべて「歌舞伎」になってしまう。歌舞伎というフィルターを通して、すべての物事を処理できてしまうんですね。最近は、『ONE PIECE』や『NARUTO -ナルト-』といったマンガ原作の作品も舞台化しているんですが、私たちが演じると、どうしても歌舞伎になってしまうんですよ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――今でこそ歌舞伎は伝統芸能と思われているけど、江戸時代に遡ってみればファッション、音楽、風俗などの最先端を積極的に取り入れてきたものでしたからね"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "廣松 そういう「最先端」を取り入れることを嫌がる、ちょっと保守的な方もいらっしゃるけど、役者自身は何とも思っていないことが多いんですよ。基本的に歌舞伎は大衆芸能ですから、「お客さんに喜んでいただけるのならば、何でもあり」なんです"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――21世紀の今、日本発のマスカルチャーといえば、アニメだったりウルトラマンや仮面ライダーなどのヒーローものだったりするわけですが、そういう意味では、歌舞伎との親和性は高かったりするわけですね。戦前に名優といわれた十五代目市村羽左衛門さんは祖先にフランス人がいたという説もありますし、歌舞伎という世界は、一般的に思われているよりも柔軟で懐が深いのかもしれません"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "「歌舞伎役者は意外と『新しいもの』に違和感がない」と廣松さん", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w5.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展示風景。黄土水《釈迦出山》 1997年鋳造（1926年の石膏原型に基づく） 台北市立美術館蔵", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "廣松 台湾でも今、日本のアニメが人気なのだということは聞きます。黄さんもアニメなどを見ていらっしゃったんですか"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 私はあまり関心がなかったですね。日本のアニメばかりが人気で、台湾オリジナルのキャラクターがあまり育たない現状は、ちょっと問題があるかな、とは思っていますけど。最近では台湾人の漫画家も増えてきて、彼らも頑張っているとは思います"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "廣松 そういうところを見ていても、日本と台湾の人たちとは同じ東アジアの住民として、通じ合うところがあると思うんですよ。繰り返しにはなりますが、だからこそ、今回の展覧会には学ぶべきところが多いと思っています"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展示風景。〈故郷／私 とはなにか〉", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/w7.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "陳澄波《緑の面をかぶった裸婦》 1929～1933年 個人蔵", "credit": "美術展ナビ"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――展覧会全体を見て、この時代の台湾と日本の交流について思うことはありますか"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 展覧会を開くきっかけになったのは、1930年代に生まれた台湾の詩人グループ「風車詩社」に興味を持ったことでした。シュールレアリスムを台湾の文壇に持ち込んだといわれる「風車詩社」ですが、この時代、台湾の表現者たちは、日本というフィルターを通して、様々なスタイルを試しているんですよね。それを西洋の分類方法で整理してしまっていいものなのか。それはちょっと安易すぎるのではないか、と思うんですよ。当時の日本と台湾が、どういう形でどういう交流をしていたのか。その実態をそのままの形で見てほしい。「西洋的な概念」はいったん忘れて、観覧してくださる方それぞれの考えで、それらの交流がどんなものだったのかを捉えなおしてほしい、そんなことを思っています"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "廣松 そういう黄さんの考えを反映しているのでしょう、それぞれの作品の解説も、わかりやすく丁寧ですけど、あまり特定の考え方を入れない、フラットな感じになっていますよね。日本人アーティストと台湾人アーティストがどのような関係にあったのか、その繋がりもわかりやすかった"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄 article_text:
今回の「特別ルポ」は、東京都現代美術館の「共時的星叢──時を共にした星たち 越境する芸術のまなざし」。前回から続く歌舞伎役者の大谷廣松さんとゲストキュレーターの黄亜歴さんとの対話だが、伝統芸能の継承者である廣松さんにとって、ここで紹介される「伝統と革新」というテーマは身近な存在。そこをひとつのキーワードとして、話は広がっていった。（文・田中聡、写真・青山謙太郎、通訳・白仕偉）

――「特別ルポ」を担当していただいている大谷廣松さんは歌舞伎役者であり、21世紀の今、伝統を継承しながらリアルタイムの芸能の現場に身を置く存在でもあります。黄さんは歌舞伎をご覧になったことはありますか？

黄 日本の伝統的な文化芸能には興味がありますし、それがどんなふうに発展し、現在存在しているかも、知りたいと思っています。だから歌舞伎の舞台はぜひ見たいですね

――歌舞伎の世界を舞台にした映画『国宝』（李相日監督）が昨年公開されまして、日本だけでなくいろいろな国で話題になっているんですが、ご覧になりましたか？

黄 日本に来る飛行機の中で見ました。結構長い映画なんですが、フライトの時間にはちょうどよかった感じで（笑）。見ていて思ったのは、伝統ある社会に新しい風が入るとき、どんな風に対処していたのだろうか、ということ。この映画の舞台となっている時代だけでなく、現代でもそういう状況はあると思いますので、そこにも興味を持ちました

――「伝統」と「革新」、このふたつをどのように両立させるか、ということですね

廣松 歌舞伎独特の「家」というシステムが、それに対する答えのひとつだと思います。役者の「家」で育つ私たちは、自然に芝居、というか歌舞伎が体に染み込んでいるんです。だからというか何というか、新しいもの、「革新」に対する抵抗感はほとんどないんです。私たちがその「革新」を舞台上に持ち込んで、それを作品に取り入れたとしても、出来上がったものはすべて「歌舞伎」になってしまう。歌舞伎というフィルターを通して、すべての物事を処理できてしまうんですね。最近は、『ONE PIECE』や『NARUTO -ナルト-』といったマンガ原作の作品も舞台化しているんですが、私たちが演じると、どうしても歌舞伎になってしまうんですよ

――今でこそ歌舞伎は伝統芸能と思われているけど、江戸時代に遡ってみればファッション、音楽、風俗などの最先端を積極的に取り入れてきたものでしたからね

廣松 そういう「最先端」を取り入れることを嫌がる、ちょっと保守的な方もいらっしゃるけど、役者自身は何とも思っていないことが多いんですよ。基本的に歌舞伎は大衆芸能ですから、「お客さんに喜んでいただけるのならば、何でもあり」なんです

――21世紀の今、日本発のマスカルチャーといえば、アニメだったりウルトラマンや仮面ライダーなどのヒーローものだったりするわけですが、そういう意味では、歌舞伎との親和性は高かったりするわけですね。戦前に名優といわれた十五代目市村羽左衛門さんは祖先にフランス人がいたという説もありますし、歌舞伎という世界は、一般的に思われているよりも柔軟で懐が深いのかもしれません

廣松 台湾でも今、日本のアニメが人気なのだということは聞きます。黄さんもアニメなどを見ていらっしゃったんですか

黄 私はあまり関心がなかったですね。日本のアニメばかりが人気で、台湾オリジナルのキャラクターがあまり育たない現状は、ちょっと問題があるかな、とは思っていますけど。最近では台湾人の漫画家も増えてきて、彼らも頑張っているとは思います

廣松 そういうところを見ていても、日本と台湾の人たちとは同じ東アジアの住民として、通じ合うところがあると思うんですよ。繰り返しにはなりますが、だからこそ、今回の展覧会には学ぶべきところが多いと思っています

――展覧会全体を見て、この時代の台湾と日本の交流について思うことはありますか

黄 展覧会を開くきっかけになったのは、1930年代に生まれた台湾の詩人グループ「風車詩社」に興味を持ったことでした。シュールレアリスムを台湾の文壇に持ち込んだといわれる「風車詩社」ですが、この時代、台湾の表現者たちは、日本というフィルターを通して、様々なスタイルを試しているんですよね。それを西洋の分類方法で整理してしまっていいものなのか。それはちょっと安易すぎるのではないか、と思うんですよ。当時の日本と台湾が、どういう形でどういう交流をしていたのか。その実態をそのままの形で見てほしい。「西洋的な概念」はいったん忘れて、観覧してくださる方それぞれの考えで、それらの交流がどんなものだったのかを捉えなおしてほしい、そんなことを思っています

廣松 そういう黄さんの考えを反映しているのでしょう、それぞれの作品の解説も、わかりやすく丁寧ですけど、あまり特定の考え方を入れない、フラットな感じになっていますよね。日本人アーティストと台湾人アーティストがどのような関係にあったのか、その繋がりもわかりやすかった

黄 日本統治時代の台湾ではいろんな制限があり、日本人と台湾人の地位も違いました。日本へ渡航すること自体も大変で、難しいことでした。その当時、台湾の農民の生活は豊かではなく、むしろ苦しんだ人が多かったのです。文学者の頼和はそれを見て胸を痛め、彼らの生活を書きました。当時は豊かな人、貧しい人、色んな階級の人たちがいて、それぞれの創作・作品がありました。金銭的に余裕がなくても、スポンサーがついて創作を続けることで、生活に困らない人たちもいました。展覧会では、それらの状況をそのまま提示して「共時的」というメッセージを伝えたいのです

廣松 そういう考えがフラットな感じのもとになっているわけですね。今まで見た美術展とは、また違った形で知性や感性を刺激してくれる展覧会でした。私にとっても面白い体験ができたと思っています（おわり）

Series competition (Previously Professional competition)

The Series competition rewards outstanding projects and narrative excellence. Enter your best series of 5 to 10 images - you could win $25,000, a solo exhibition, a range of top Sony Digital Imaging equipment plus benefit from international media exposure.

Free to enter

Open to anyone submitting a series of 5 to 10 images per category

Ten diverse categories to enter

Awards for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place photographers plus up to 7 shortlisted photographers per category

One overall winner receives the Photographer of the Year title

Please see 'Rules' below for full image eligibility criteria

Photographer of the Year is rewarded with a solo presentation of their work as part of the Sony World Photography Awards London exhibition the following year

Deadline is January 12 2027 at 16.00 GMT

PRIZES

**Might be digital depending on position

Rules

The Series competition rewards outstanding projects and narrative excellence. Photographers must submit a minimum of five (5) and a maximum of ten (10) images and all submissions must be accompanied by a series description.

If you enter the Series competition, you can also enter the Single Image competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

1.1 By entering the Competition, You agree and acknowledge that the World Photography Organisation is permitted to receive your registration data. All personal information will be used by the World Photography Organisation by its Privacy Policy.

1.2.1 The Competition is free to enter.

1.2.2 The Series competition is open to all Photographers entering a body of work.

1.3 All Entrants must be over 18.

1.4 By entering the Competition You hereby accept these Competition Rules and the Terms and Conditions.

1.5 Entries must be submitted by 12 January, 2027 at 16.00 GMT

1.6 If you enter the Series competition, you can also enter the Single Image competition. Entrants choosing to submit work across both Single Image and Series competitions must choose work originating from different bodies of work.

2. To enter, you must upload your image via the World Photography Organisation website ( www.worldphoto.org ) or any of the official Sony World Photography Awards’ website and follow the on-screen instructions carefully.

2.1 Image Entry criteria:

Published work may have been taken at any point in history, but must have been published between the dates of 1 January 2026 and 12 January 2027.

Up to 20% of work can be published at any point in time on your personal website, social media or exhibited as part of an official programme i.e. two images can be published on personal platforms at any point in time if submitting a series of 8-10 images. One image can be published at any point in time if submitting a series of 5-7 images.

Un-published work entered into the competition may have been taken at any point in history but never been shown publicly. Once unpublished work has been entered, it cannot be entered again as published work in the future year of the Awards’ competition.

2.2 Images should be no smaller than 1MB and no larger than 5MB. Images should be JPEG files.

All images must be saved in the sRGB colour model and EXIF data must be left in the image file.

All Entrants, if they are selected amongst the shortlist, must be able to supply a high resolution image suitable for printing in exhibitions should the image be required.

3.1 Entries will be judged between January 13, 2027 and January 31, 2027.

3.2 The three finalists (1st, 2nd and 3rd place) and a shortlist of up to seven photographers from each category will be selected and announced prior to April 2027. Category winners and overall competition winners will be announced in April 2027. The finalists and shortlist will be notified by email in January.

3.3.1 The winner of each category will be notified by email

3.4 The decision of the Judges and the World Photography Organisation is final and no negotiation will be entered into with respect to any such decision.

3.5 You may enter a minimum of five (5) and a maximum of ten (10) images per category, and may enter as many categories as you wish, however you cannot enter the same series or images into more than one category.

3.5.1 Judging will be based on the portfolio of work entered for each category.

3.5.2. During the judging process successful entries may be moved to a different category to the category they originally entered into. The decision will be made at the discretion of the judging panel. Successful entrants will be notified of the change over email.

4. Your Entry may feature manipulation, but where Entries are manipulated, the extent of which must be described in the image description section when submitting. For the avoidance of doubt, all Entries must originally be from either an analogue or digital photograph which may have then been manipulated. Computer generated content cannot be the origin of the Entry. Should a question arise through the judging process regarding the extent of your Entry’s manipulation you may be requested to submit the original photograph and image file to verify.

4.1 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to disqualify and remove any entry that does not comply with the following requirements, even after the entry is submitted on the Website. You warrant and represent, in respect of each entry submitted by You (“Entry”), as follows:

4.1.1 You are the sole owner and author of each Entry

4.1.2 You have the right to make Your Entry available to the Competition

4.1.3 Each Entry does not contain personally identifiable information about you or any other person(s)

4.1.4 Each Entry does not contain any infringing, threatening, false, misleading, abusive, harassing, libellous,defamatory, vulgar, obscene, scandalous, inflammatory, pornographic or profane content

4.1.5 Each Entry does not contain any material that could constitute or encourage conduct that would be considered a criminal offence, give rise to civil liability, or otherwise violate any law

4.1.6 Each Entry does not infringe upon the copyrights, trademarks, contract rights, or any other intellectual property rights of any third person or entity, or violate any person’s rights of privacy or publicity, including:

4.1.6.1 trademarks owned by third parties

4.1.6.2 copyrighted materials owned by third parties (including movie dialogue or musical compositions)

4.1.6.3 names, likenesses, voices or other characteristics identifying celebrities or other public figures, living or dead

4.1.7 Entries which contain any commercial content that promotes any product or service other than that of the World Photography Organisation.

4.1.8 Entries containing screen credits

4.1.9 No animals were harmed, manipulated or distressed in the making of the image. This includes, but is not limited to:

Deliberately disturbing or provoking an animal to capture a reaction

Using tape lures or decoys to attract animals or trigger a behaviour

Live baiting of any kind

Using flash photography on nocturnal birds

Failing to adhere to applicable laws, rules and permissions when working with wildlife and in natural environments, for example with protected species or protected environments

4.1.10 Archival images may be used when creating new work where any usage maintains compliance with clause 2. All archival images must be used with the required permissions. Usage of archival images must be stated in the description. 4.1.11 Drone usage must comply with the laws, rules, and permissions of the country in which the image was taken. The Promoter may request proof of permissions where applicable.

4.2 You agree to fully indemnify the World Photography Organisation in respect of all royalties, fees and any other monies owing to any person by reason of Your breaching any of the foregoing.

4.3 You confirm that each person depicted in the Entry has granted permission to be portrayed as shown. Any costumes, props or other materials used must be rented or borrowed with the permission of the owner, and all other relevant permissions must have been obtained.

4.4 In accordance with clause 3.2 and 3.3 all shortlisted and winning photographers will be contacted by email. If the World Photography Organisation does not hear from the entrant by the date specified in any correspondence and is therefore not able to ratify the entry that entrant will be disqualified and replaced by another photographer.

5. Intentionally deleted.

6. The World Photography Organisation may run an online rating process whereby members of the public may vote for a favourite photograph. If there is sufficient evidence (in the World Photography Organisation’s sole discretion) to suggest malpractice and manipulation of the rating process, then the World Photography Organisation has the right to remove the relevant Entry or Entries and, if necessary, award the prize to a different Entrant. The decisions of the World Photography Organisation are final.

7.1 The World Photography Organisation recognises You, the author of the image, retain full ownership of the copyright in each Entry.

7.2 All Entrants understand that any image submitted to the Competition may be used by the World Photography Organisation, and its Event Partners, for marketing and promotional purposes of You the author and the Event only, for a maximum of three years after April 2027. Please refer to clause 7.4. You hereby grant the World Photography Organisation a non-exclusive, irrevocable licence in each Entry throughout the world for three years in all media for any use connected to the promotion of You the author and the Sony World Photography Awards Event and/or Competition, including, but not limited too:

(a) judging the Competition

(b) displaying the winning and shortlisted entries at public exhibitions promoting the World Photography Organisation and organised by the World Photography Organisation

(c) inclusion within the Website, a World Photography Awards book, magazine or similar

(d) inclusion within any materials promoting of the Competition and / or any exhibition organised by the World Photography Organisation, in the promotion of the World Photography Organisation

(e) inclusion on Competition- and exhibition-related products to be sold by the World Photography Organisation or any third party following the individual agreement by the author

(f) sub-licensing the Entries to the press for reproduction in connection with the Competition and any exhibition

(g) allowing viewers of the Website to view images on a computer screen, PDA or mobile telephone and store such pages in electronic form on disk or on a PDA or mobile telephone (but not on any server or other storage device connected to a network) for their personal, non-commercial use only. Please also refer to clause 9.

7.3 All Entrants understand that the image information, including image name and description, may be shared with Event Partners and media as per clause 7.1, 7.2 and 8. For the avoidance of doubt the “image information” does not include any personal information of You the author.

7.3.1 Should entrants elect to opt-in to sharing data, the email data and name will be shared with our event partners.

7.4 For media purposes in accordance with clause 7.2 and to promote your winning images the World Photography Organisation will choose a maximum of two to three images, from the series entered for media use; should media require further images for publication this will be done in consultation with You.

7.5 The World Photography Organisation reserves the right to select which images from within the winning series that will be featured within the curated exhibit and such curation is made in its sole discretion. Associated series descriptions, image captions and bios may also be edited to fit within the context of the exhibition, book or other material connected to the Awards .

7.6 All entrants are required to enter under their correct names, and all entrants are responsible for providing this information accurately. The Awards programme is structured around providing opportunities and exposure to individual photographers and as such we do not award anonymously or accept pseudonyms.

7.7 For Entrants that qualify for the National & Regional Award programme, the Promoter reserves the right not to award a winner if, in the opinion of the judges, none of the Entrants meet the required standard.

8. Any photograph used by the World Photography Organisation shall carry a credit line. Any failure to provide such credit line shall not be deemed to be a breach, as long as the World Photography Organisation uses its reasonable endeavours to rectify such failure within a reasonable period from the date of notice of such failure.

8a. All entrants understand the World Photography Organisation may need to crop your image or add text or logos when used specifically to promote your work or the Awards for online promotional purposes only.

9. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any incorrect, inaccurate or incomplete information, whether caused by website users or by any of the equipment or programming associated with or utilised in the Competition, and the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for technical, hardware or software failure of any kind, for lost network connections, garbled computer transmissions, other problems or technical malfunctions with regard to the Competition. The World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility for any error, omission, corruption, interruption, deletion, defect, delay in operation or transmission, communications line failure, theft or destruction or unauthorized access to or alteration of Entries. The World Photography Organisation is not responsible for any problems or technical malfunction of any telephone network or lines, computer on-line systems, servers, computer equipment, software, failure of any e-mail addressed to the World Photography Organisation on account of technical problems, human error or traffic congestion on the internet or any website, or any combination thereof, including any injury or damage to Your or any other person's computer related to or resulting from participation or downloading any materials in the Competition. If for any reason a contestant’s entry cannot be viewed or is not capable of running as planned, including infection by computer viruses, bugs, tampering, unauthorized intervention, fraud or technical failures, the World Photography Organisation assumes no responsibility.

10. In no event will the World Photography Organisation, its parents, affiliates, subsidiaries and related companies, Event Partners, its advertising or promotion agencies, or its officers, directors, employees, shareholders, representatives or agents be responsible or liable for any damages or losses of any kind, including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages arising out of any Entrant’s access to and use of the Website. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, everything on the Website is provided "as is"without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied, including but not limited to, the implied warranty of merchantability, fitness for purpose or use or non-infringement.

11. You agree to participate in related publicity and to the use of Your name and likeness for the purposes of advertising, promotion and publicity without additional compensation.

12. If shortlisted entrants are unable to supply a high resolution image of at least 5MB and 300ppi their entry may be disqualified.

13. There are no cash alternatives available for prize winners.

13.1 Prize winners may receive digital imaging equipment as part of their prize and in such cases equipment may be sent to them. In some countries income tax may be applicable to prizes. It is the winner’s responsibility to pay any income taxes related to the prize in compliance with their own country’s law. In such cases the Winner agrees to indemnify and keep the World Photography Organisation, its parents, affiliates or partners indemnified against any tax liability, charges, fines, penalties or interest or any other liability incurred by the winner which liability arose as a result of prizes provided to the Winner.

13.1.i Valid ETAs or Standard Visas to the UK are needed to attend the ceremony. It is the responsibility of the Entrant to acquire their own visa or entry forms. The Promoter is not responsible for the cost of the Entrant’s visa application and entry forms.

13.2 The Photographer of the Year prize offers the winner a solo presentation at the Sony World Photography Awards exhibition at Somerset House the following year. The exhibited images must comply with the World Photography Organisation’s rules. The winner will work closely with the World Photography Organisation and the exhibition curator on the allocated space, presentation and curation of the exhibition. Final decisions on space, production and cost remains with the World Photography Organisation. Any associated travel and accommodation costs will not be covered by the World Photography Organisation.

14. Winners will be announced online and at a black-tie ceremony in London.

Promoter: World Photography Organisation, Creo Arts Group Limited, 9 Manchester Square, London, United Kingdom.

article_text:
Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (Zeitz MOCAA) presents Afflict the Comfortable, Comfort the Afflicted , a survey exhibition by Los Angeles–based artist Cauleen Smith . Curated by Thato Mogotsi, Curator of Contemporary Art at Zeitz MOCAA, the exhibition opens on Thursday, 20 November 2025, on Level 3 Silo Side, and runs until Sunday, 11 October 2026.

In her first major presentation on the African continent , Smith’s world-building projects come together in atmospheric installations that offer visitors a layered sensory experience. Short films and videos interact with drawings, sculpted objects, colourful textile banners and the sonic in an expansive exhibition that meditates on the artist’s ongoing concern with Black experimental cinema, Afrocentric aesthetics, Black feminism and the emancipatory uses of the utopic. Smith’s decades-long practice merges her interests in jazz and literature, spirituality, feminism, Afrofuturism and what she calls ‘…the everyday possibilities of the imagination.’

Curator Thato Mogotsi explains: ‘ Afflict the Comfortable, Comfort the Afflicted extends beyond a survey of Cauleen Smith’s practice; it’s an invitation to imagine generosity as a radical act. Smith’s work demonstrates how rarely engaged archives – explored through the moving image and the sonic – can offer unlikely moments of relation, refuge and resistance. In bringing her world to Zeitz MOCAA, we also foreground a dialogue about how Black imagination continues to shape the ways we see, feel, and gather—across time, and across geographies.’

Smith is a prolific and widely recognised filmmaker and multidisciplinary artist whose practice engages with non-Western cosmologies, Afro-diasporic histories, and pan-African cultural icons. Interrelated bodies of work are inspired by post-Katrina New Orleans; Afrofuturist musician Sun Ra ; Malian photographer Malick Sidibé ; and legendary jazz musician and devotional leader Alice Coltrane-Turiyasangitananda , among others. It is within their journeys and the landscapes they navigated that Smith’s own speculative interest in the utopic potential of Black gathering and placemaking emerges.

Smith first came to prominence in the 1990s as part of a generation of filmmakers challenging Hollywood’s limited portrayals of Black life. Her debut feature film, Drylongso (1998), was celebrated at the Sundance Film Festival and, in 2023, was re-released in a 4K restoration by the renowned film archive, Criterion Collection , reaffirming its enduring cultural significance.

The exhibition’s title references one of Smith’s text-based banners, inspired by Paul Thek’s 1985 painting of the same name , which in turn borrows the phrase coined by American writer and humorist Finley Peter Dunne to describe the role of the press in society. Smith subverts this phrase, transforming it into a call to action —one that urges us to extend collective care as a form of creative resistance, while unsettling systems of privilege and power.

Featured works include Smith’s celebrated films A Woman Discusses Her Skirt (2008), Remote Viewing (2011), Pilgrim (2017), and Sojourner (2018). These films traverse the cultural and storied urban landscapes of Los Angeles, New Orleans, Texas and Chicago, honouring figures and communities whose contributions to liberatory traditions continue to sustain Black life. Her films reject the constraints of linear time, instead tracing unexpected connections across history, memory, and imagination.

The exhibition’s spatial design reflects Smith’s intertextual and research-driven approach , drawing on longstanding forms of Black expression. Through sound, light, and a sensorial filmic style, Smith invites viewers to consider what becomes possible when movement, gathering, and the quest for Black utopias are placed at the centre of our collective imagination.

In a recent profile, the artist Cauleen Smith reflects: ‘I know that art is powerful and that it can be used for change. But I think its real power is in the way it resists everything that is about power. The potency of art comes from the way in which it doesn’t need any power to affect you. It doesn’t have to coerce you. It doesn’t have to force you to do anything. It extends itself and then people come towards it.’

Afflict the Comfortable, Comfort the Afflicted forms part of Zeitz MOCAA’s ongoing series of in-depth, research-based solo exhibitions that highlight and contextualise the practices of important artists from Africa and its Diaspora. In this spirit of radical solidarity, the museum continues to look beyond the continent’s borders—examining the ways the world is implicated in Africa, and Africa in the world.

This exhibition is made possible through support from the Terra Foundation for American Art. Zeitz MOCAA’s exhibition and curatorial programming is generously supported by the Mellon Foundation and BMW South Africa.

meet the artist

Cauleen Smith

Cauleen Smith (b. Riverside, California, 1967) is a filmmaker and artist who lives and works in Los Angeles, California. With a BA in cinema from San Francisco State University (1991) and an MFA in filmmaking from the University of California-Los Angeles (1998). Her interdisciplinary work expands from histories and practices of experimental film, including structuralism, Third World cinema, and science fiction.

Smith’s works have been featured in solo exhibitions at institutions such as Los Angeles County Museum of Art, Los Angeles, CA; Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, NY; Institute of Contemporary Art, Philadelphia, PA; San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, San Francisco, CA; Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, Chicago, IL; Art Institute of Chicago, Chicago, IL; Massachusetts Museum of Contemporary Art, North Adams, MA; Contemporary Arts Museum Houston, Houston, TX; Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, PA and the Astrup Fearnley Museet, Oslo, Norway among others. Smith has received numerous grants and awards, including a Heinz Award and a Guggenheim Fellowship.

Her films screen internationally, and her works are in public collections around the world, including the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, the Museum of Arts and Design in New York, the Smithsonian American Art Museum in Washington and the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

article_text:
Films and events

Cult

Nightborn

A couple’s dream of idyllic family life in the Finnish woods is shattered by the arrival of their nightmarish new baby, in Hanna Bergholm’s riotously gory folk horror.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Hanna Bergholm

Screenwriters Hanna Bergholm, Ilja Rautsi

With Seidi Haarla, Rupert Grint

Finland-Lithuania-France-UK 2026. 92min

Courtesy of Shudder

Languages English, Finnish With some English subtitles

Introduction

Drawing deeply from the wells of folk horror and psychological post-natal angst, director Bergholm pits Seidi Haarla and Rupert Grint’s new parents against their hairy, howling offspring, which displays a taste for raw meat over milk. Gruesome and bloody, it’s also chock-full of self-aware humour that surely guarantees the film’s place as a future cult classic.

Leigh Singer

With thanks to Finnish Institute.

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and harm towards children.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Hot Spot

The new film from the acclaimed director of The Silent Twins is a daring and distinctive sci-fi thriller set in a near-future society ruled by sentient AI.

The Face of Horror

In this stunning, blood-soaked homage to Technicolor horror films, a woman in medieval England rises from the grave to wreak revenge on her husband.

Godzilla Minus Zero

The sequel to Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed 2023 film is a true cinematic spectacle that’s sure to grip fans of Godzilla, as well as newcomers to the franchise.
